alignments.note: Construct noun keeps only its own word. The accepted alignment additionally gave it *have* as a recast construct relation, but MACULA tags s002 רֵיחַ `Ncmsa` (absolute) and s003 `Ncmpc`, so no construct relation between fragrance and oils stands in the projection and s003 is the regens rather than the rectum; rule 43 places the *have* elsewhere.

The ASV recasts the clause possessively (*Thine oils have a goodly fragrance*). No הָיָה stands here, no written verb is rendered by *have*, and the suffix already holds *Thine*, so under rule 43's counting rider it is not a home for a second word; the לְ is the clause's one relational morpheme on which the ASV has spent nothing, and the *have* is what it is rendered by, exactly as `שָׁפְרָה עָלָי` → *I have a goodly heritage* gives *goodly* to the adjective and *have* to the preposition. Two materially available alternatives: *have* `added` under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause, and *have* folded into שְׁמָנֶי as a recast construct relation (the accepted reading). The `added` branch is rejected because rule 43 reaches it only where no preposition or suffix is left with an English word to take, and this preposition is.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'And our rafters are firs' with a single plural noun and no textual note attached to it; the three notes on this verse are all classed alternative_rendering (houses / of cedar . . . of fir / cypresses) and bear on English wording, not on the reading here. The qere rahitenu and the ketiv rhytnw differ only in the he/heth of the consonantal spelling and yield the same word 'our rafters', so no ASV wording can distinguish them. Both readings remain compatible and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
